persona.who: 49, IT services manager in Pune, 22 years in the same company, laid off last month. Daughter in 11th, home loan, aging mother.
persona.note: twenty two years in one company and they let me go in a 10 minute call. I have not told my mother. Every morning I still wake up at 6 like I have to go to office.

understanding.bridge: The verdict was delivered in ten minutes, but the sentence you keep living is not theirs to write. What you are is not a role they can revoke.
understanding.week_thesis: Seven days from carrying the shame of a call to standing in the man you are, not the employee they ended.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the disbelief and the shame of a call that ended what you built, named without judgement.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that the only thing they took was the title, and the rest is still yours.
week_beats.act: You try telling one person the truth, and you begin the next morning as the man you are, not the employee they ended.
week_beats.story: A man of long service who was dismissed and carried the shame alone shows you what standing in your own worth looks like.

understanding.core_struggle: After twenty-two years, was let go in a call, and is carrying the shame alone without telling his mother.
understanding.mirror: You still wake at six for a job that ended, and the silence you keep from your mother is heavier than the call was.
understanding.insight: The call was a business decision, not a verdict on your worth. The shame you carry is the only thing they actually took from you, and it is yours to put down.

queries.hook: Being let go after twenty-two years and carrying the shame alone, still waking as if the job were real.
queries.diagnose: When a role is taken away, the mind turns the loss into a verdict on the self; the harm is not the ending but the story you tell about it.
queries.steady: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what they decided; your worth was never theirs to grant or revoke.
queries.act: Lift yourself up, do not push yourself down; speak the truth to one person you trust, and begin the next morning as the man you are, not the employee they ended.
queries.story: A man of long service who was dismissed and carried the shame alone, who found that his worth was never in the title they held.

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
verse.sanskrit: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥
verse.line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
verse.translation: For the mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, powerful and stubborn. I think it is as hard to hold as the wind.
verse.why: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

matched.label: I feel anxious most of the time

prasang.title: Mastering the mind
prasang.summary: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.
prasang.lesson: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

verse.meaning: Arjuna tells Krishna that the mind is restless and stubborn, as hard to hold as the wind. Krishna agrees and says that practice and letting go can train it. This means the mind does not obey you by force. It resists, it wanders, it storms. But it can be shaped by returning to it again and again, by noticing when it leaves and guiding it back without forcing.
verse.for_you: The ten-minute call took your role, not your worth. The shame you feel is a storm in the mind, not the truth of who you are. Let the mind be wild today. Do not fight the disbelief. Just let it move.

verse.speaker: Janaka
verse.setting: King Janaka, alone on his palace roof after overhearing wandering sages, rethinks his life.
verse.sanskrit: संपदश्च विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेच्चित्तेन संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा हन्त मन्ये महापदः ॥ आपदोऽपि विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेन्मनसि संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा मन्ये मनसि संपदः ॥
verse.line: Good fortune the mind clutches becomes trouble. Trouble the mind accepts becomes a kind of fortune.
verse.translation: All those dazzling fortunes, if the mind clings to them, are really great calamities in grand disguise. And all those varied misfortunes, if the mind accepts them, are really fortunes.
verse.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.
verse.misuse: Accepting a hardship doesn't mean not fixing what can be fixed.

matched.label: I can't handle not knowing what comes next

prasang.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
prasang.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
prasang.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
prasang.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

verse.meaning: King Janaka, alone on his palace roof after hearing wandering sages, questions everything he has built. He sees that the mind holds the power to turn fortune into disaster and disaster into fortune. A title or a loss is only a circumstance. The mind can clutch at what is gone and make it a ruin, or it can accept the fact of it and walk on. The work of the day does not change. Only the way the mind holds it changes.
verse.for_you: What is real in you cannot be taken or lost; only what changes can be taken, and you are more than what changes.

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: Ashtavakra presses home his core teaching to Janaka: you are awareness, not the roles you play.
verse.sanskrit: त्वय्यनन्तमहाम्भोधौ विश्ववीचिः स्वभावतः । उदेतु वास्तमायातु न ते वृद्धिर्न वा क्षतिः ॥
verse.line: Let the waves of the world rise or fall. You, the ocean, neither gain nor lose.
verse.translation: In you, the boundless ocean, let the waves of the world rise or fall by their own nature. You neither grow nor shrink.
verse.why: You are the ocean, not the waves; let them rise and fall without losing yourself.

prasang.title: You are not your mind
prasang.summary: Ashtavakra drives home that Janaka is not the body, the doer, or the mind's likes and dislikes, but the ocean in which the waves of life rise and fall. He urges faith, an end to grief, and rest from endless deliberation.
prasang.lesson: You are the ocean, not the waves; let them rise and fall without losing yourself.

verse.meaning: Ashtavakra speaks to Janaka, who is caught in the roles of ruler and father, and says let the world's waves rise and fall. You are the ocean, not the waves. You neither grow nor shrink. The work ends, the body ages, the children leave, but the ground beneath it all remains. The ten-minute call is a wave, and it falls.
verse.for_you: Do what you can today, take refuge in what does not change, and meet each moment with courage instead of rehearsing the worst.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: निन्दन्तु नीतिनिपुणा यदि वा स्तुवन्तु लक्ष्मीः समाविशतु गच्छतु वा यथेष्टम् । अद्यैव वा मरणमस्तु युगान्तरे वा न्याय्यात्पथः प्रविचलन्ति पदं न धीराः ॥
verse.line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
verse.translation: Let the worldly-wise blame or praise; let fortune come or go as she pleases; let death come today or ages hence: the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right.
verse.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari is speaking to you, the reader, from the section on steadfastness. They have just told you that after twenty-two years, they were let go in a ten-minute call, and each morning they still wake at six as if the job exists. The verse says let the worldly-wise blame or praise. Let fortune come or go. The steadfast do not move a step from the right path. You are not that call, and the path you walk does not end where their offer letter did.
verse.for_you: The shame of that ten-minute call is heavy, but it does not erase the work you have done or the person you are. Let the verdict sit where it belongs, and keep your feet on the path that is yours.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
verse.sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
verse.line: Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.
verse.translation: Raise yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
verse.why: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.
verse.misuse: Not 'you're alone, so don't ask for help'. Arjuna himself asks for help; this is about not abandoning yourself.

prasang.title: Lift yourself by yourself; marks of the realised
prasang.summary: Raise yourself by yourself; you are your own friend or enemy. The self-mastered person stays calm in heat and cold, praise and blame, and sees friend and foe alike.
prasang.lesson: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield, reminding him that the self alone is both friend and enemy. The self can pull itself up by its own strength, or it can drag itself down with doubt. The one who chooses to lift is steady, while the one who pushes down is lost. This is the moment to decide which you will be.
verse.for_you: When you wake at six, the call is not there to push you down. Be the one who lifts. Make your morning coffee, look in the mirror, and say to yourself that the man who raised his children and cared for his parents is not a role they can end.

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on how a free person moves through the world.
verse.sanskrit: प्राप्तकर्मकरो नित्यं शत्रुमित्रसमानदृक् । ईहितानीहितैर्मुक्तो न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ॥ सर्वस्याभिमतं वक्ता चोदितः पेशलोक्तिमान् । आशयज्ञश्च भूतानां संसारे नावसीदति ॥
verse.line: Do the work in front of you, speak gently, read people's hearts, and you won't sink in the world.
verse.translation: Always doing the work that comes, seeing friend and foe alike, free of wanting and not-wanting, such a one neither grieves nor craves. Saying what is agreeable to all, speaking gently when asked, knowing the intent of others' hearts, such a one does not sink in the world.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.meaning: Ribhu tells Nidagha how a free person lives in the world. The student asks how to act when the world pulls at every side. The teacher answers that freedom is not escape. It is doing the work in front of you. It is speaking gently when asked. It is reading the hearts of those around you. It is seeing friend and foe with the same steady eye. When you live this way, you do not sink in the world. You do not grieve what is lost. You do not crave what is not yours.
verse.for_you: Tomorrow morning at six, let the alarm sound. You will not reach for a phone to read messages from the company. You will make your tea and sit with it. That is the work in front of you. It is small and it is yours.

story.title: Ram accepts exile
story.story_hook: He went to the palace to be crowned and came out with fourteen years in the forest.
story.summary: On the morning of his coronation, Ram is summoned and told by Kaikeyi that he must go into the forest for fourteen years. He agrees without anger, and is hurt only that his father could not tell him himself. He walks out showing no change of mind, already thinking of those he must comfort.
story.lesson: You cannot control the news; you can control the person who walks out of the room.

anchor.speaker: Narrator
anchor.setting: Ram walks out of the palace, having lost the throne he was to receive that morning.
anchor.sanskrit: न वनं गन्तुकामस्य त्यजतश्च वसुंधराम्। सर्वलोकातिगस्येव लक्ष्यते चित्तविक्रिया॥
anchor.line: He had just lost the kingdom, and his mind showed no change at all.
anchor.translation: As he set out for the forest and gave up the earth, no change could be seen in his mind, as if he stood beyond the world.
anchor.why: You cannot control the news; you can control the person who walks out of the room.
anchor.misuse: Calm in loss is not pretending it does not hurt; Ram grieves elsewhere in the story.

prasang.title: Ram accepts exile
prasang.summary: On the morning of his coronation, Ram is summoned and told by Kaikeyi that he must go into the forest for fourteen years. He agrees without anger, and is hurt only that his father could not tell him himself. He walks out showing no change of mind, already thinking of those he must comfort.
prasang.story_hook: He went to the palace to be crowned and came out with fourteen years in the forest.
prasang.lesson: You cannot control the news; you can control the person who walks out of the room.

story.hook_title: Ram went to be crowned and came out exiled for fourteen years
story.teaser: Ram went to be crowned and came out exiled for fourteen years
story.for_you: Ram walked out of the palace after losing the kingdom, and his mind showed no change. You can let the ten-minute call be the end of a role without letting it rewrite the man who wakes at six and carries his parents and children.

script: You wake at six and your body waits for a call that will never come. The silence in the room is loud. You are carrying a disbelief that feels heavier than the morning itself.
Arjuna has just spoken. He has told Krishna that the mind is restless and stubborn. Arjuna said:
चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम्, तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम्.
In plain words: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.

Krishna agrees that the mind is hard to hold. He does not promise to calm it by force. He says practice and letting go can train it. This is easier said than done, because you cannot simply command your thoughts to stop. The mind resists. It storms. It wanders. But it can be shaped by returning to it again and again.
Let the disbelief move through you today. Do not fight the shame. Just notice when your mind storms and guide it back without forcing it. The call is over. The verdict is done.
The mind is a storm. Let it pass.

depth.life: You wake at six to a job that no longer exists. The silence in the house holds the shame of a ten-minute call, and you carry it alone while your parents grow older and your children still need you.
depth.points: The mind is a storm that no one else can hold for you. The verdict was a business decision, but the sentence you live in your head is yours to release.
depth.practice: Sit with the disbelief for five minutes without fixing it or naming it.
depth.question: What would it mean to let the storm pass without trying to calm it?
